videos.title: Nursing handoff vignette
videos.videoPrompt: 45–60s B-roll: empty treatment room, sealed tray prep, doorway handoff space without faces, honesty card about nursing cover constraints. No synthetic clinician faces labelled as WMC.

beats.voOrCaption: Nursing sits beside consulting — not as decoration, as clinical capacity.
A pathway is flagged. The nurse prepares the room, equipment, and patient information the GP will need.
The GP joins for the procedure or reviews the outcome. Documentation and recall close the loop.
Session support depends on nursing cover. That constraint is part of how we plan lists.

videos.title: Reception flow vignette
videos.videoPrompt: Reception workflow B-roll: desk, check-in counter detail, waiting-to-reception depth, honesty card. Screens blanked. No PHI.

beats.voOrCaption: Reception holds the list together — bookings, triage cues, and enquiries that should not break a consult.
Results, scripts, and referral checks are routed. Urgent same-day needs are flagged without collapsing the whole morning.
When a session runs late, patients hear it from the desk. Continuity preferences are noted for the next booking.
These are workflows that protect consulting time — not a customer-service slogan.

videos.title: Peer discussion — how we ask
videos.videoPrompt: Peer discussion vignette using corridor/doorway B-roll; talking-head beat reserved for consented GP later. Placeholder cut uses environment only.

beats.voOrCaption: Clinical questions here are short and specific — often between rooms, not in a meeting theatre.
When I am unsure, I ask a colleague or nursing. Autonomy matters — so does a second clinical mind.
Privacy stays in the exchange: no identifiable detail in the corridor; escalate into a room when needed.
This is professional peercraft — not a culture campaign.

videos.title: Continuity — what changes in the consult
videos.videoPrompt: Continuity film: waiting + empty consult atmosphere, composite framing honesty, no patient identities.

beats.voOrCaption: Continuity is not a slogan here. It is recognising change from a baseline you already hold.
Over years with the same family, the consult starts further along. You spend less time rebuilding the story and more time on what changed.
Nursing recalls and same-GP booking habits keep the thread between sessions. When continuity breaks, repair is deliberate.
